title: Spider-Man: Brand New Day Crosses ₹350 Crore in India, Set To Dethrone Avengers: Endgame as MCU's Highest-Grosser
excerpt: Tom Holland's latest Spider-Man film collected ₹351.5 crore net in just 9 days and needs only ₹21.72 crore more to surpass Avengers: Endgame's all-time MCU record in India.
body:
• Spider-Man: Brand New Day has collected ₹351.5 crore net (₹414.75 crore gross) in India after 9 days, crossing the 350 crore mark faster than any Hollywood film
  • The film needs just ₹21.72 crore more to overtake Avengers: Endgame's ₹373.22 crore and become the highest-grossing MCU film ever in India
  • Globally, Brand New Day has crossed $1.18 billion worldwide, with India emerging as one of its strongest international markets

Spider-Man: Brand New Day continued its record-breaking run at the Indian box office on day 9, collecting an estimated ₹15.5 crore net across six language versions — Hindi, English, Tamil, Telugu, Kannada, and Malayalam. The Destin Daniel Cretton-directed film has now amassed ₹351.5 crore net (₹414.75 crore gross) in India, putting Avengers: Endgame's all-time MCU record squarely in its crosshairs.

Day 9 Defies the Second-Friday Dip

In a remarkable hold, Brand New Day actually grew on its second Friday compared to the previous day's ₹15 crore. Films typically drop on their second Friday before recovering over the weekend, but Tom Holland's fourth solo outing as Peter Parker has broken that pattern. TrackTollywood's live tracking data shows the film maintaining 15.4% occupancy across 14,605 shows in 776 cities on day 9, with a 4.8% increase over the previous day.

Bengaluru has emerged as the film's top-performing city with ₹42.02 crore in gross collections, while Maharashtra leads among states at ₹84.79 crore gross. Hyderabad, which recorded 58% occupancy on opening day, and the southern markets continue to drive strong numbers.

Endgame Record Within Reach

The milestone everyone is watching: Avengers: Endgame's ₹373.22 crore net, the all-time MCU record in India since 2019. Brand New Day needs just ₹21.72 crore more — a target that should be comfortably achieved over the second weekend. Bollywood Hungama projects a lifetime collection of ₹475-480 crore, which would make it the highest-grossing Hollywood film in Indian history by a wide margin.

The film has already shattered several records. Its ₹61 crore net opening day beat Avengers: Endgame's ₹53.50 crore to become the biggest Hollywood opener in India. Its 8-day total of ₹336 crore is the highest opening week for any Hollywood film in the country.

"The film has sold around 3.75 lakh tickets in the top 3 national chains — PVRInox and Cinepolis — and is looking at a final advance in the vicinity of 5 lakh tickets for the opening day alone."

— Bollywood Hungama, on opening day advance bookings

Where It Stands Among MCU Films in India

Brand New Day has already lapped the competition among MCU titles in India. The full rankings by net collection tell the story:

Avengers: Endgame sits at ₹373.22 crore, followed by Brand New Day at ₹351.5 crore after just 9 days. The gap to third place — Avengers: Infinity War at ₹227.43 crore — is enormous. Spider-Man: No Way Home (₹212 crore), Deadpool & Wolverine (₹135 crore), and Doctor Strange in the Multiverse of Madness (₹126.94 crore) round out the top six.

Brand New Day hasn't just outperformed its MCU peers — it has done so at a pace none of them matched. The film crossed ₹300 crore in just 4 days, a feat no Hollywood release had achieved in India.

A $1.18 Billion Global Phenomenon

India's numbers are part of a worldwide juggernaut. Spider-Man: Brand New Day has grossed $1.18 billion globally — $481 million in the United States and $706 million overseas. The film, produced by Columbia Pictures, Marvel Studios, and Pascal Pictures on a $200-220 million budget, is already the highest-grossing film of 2026 worldwide.

The cast includes Tom Holland, Zendaya, Sadie Sink, Jacob Batalon, Jon Bernthal, Florence Pugh, Tramell Tillman, Michael Mando, and Mark Ruffalo. Premium 3D formats have been the biggest revenue driver in India, with the English 3D version alone contributing ₹11.44 crore on opening day.

What's Next

Day 10 is already tracking strong, with ₹16.34 crore gross collected by early afternoon on Saturday at 26.2% occupancy. Sunday advance bookings show ₹16.81 crore already locked across 13,870 shows. The Endgame record should fall by Saturday or Sunday, after which the conversation shifts to whether Brand New Day can sustain its run long enough to challenge ₹500 crore — a number no Hollywood film has ever reached in India.
